Bitcoin Tests Lows as Sentiment Sours ---------------------------------------- Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC ) fell to a four-month low after the Hidden Gems rec posted a fifth straight day of losses, with the cryptocurrency close to testing the February market bottom around $60,000, as multiple factors weigh on sentiment. * Investors have pulled nearly $4.4 billion from U.S.-listed Bitcoin ETFs over the past 13 sessions: One such reason is the first sale of Bitcoin from Strategy (NASDAQ:MSTR ) since 2022 and a reallocation of funds towards surging tech stocks, hitting ETF outflows. * Retail traders raising funds to participate in upcoming IPOs: With SpaceX set to go public next week and other major AI companies lining up public offerings, some of the outflows from crypto can be linked to liquidity needs. We don’t think AI is a bubble — but we do think it’s changing

Every new technology hits a moment where excitement cools and reality sets in. That’s usually when the real opportunities start to emerge.

That’s how we’re thinking about AI right now.

The infrastructure is largely built. The next phase is about adoption — real businesses using AI to solve real problems. And historically, that’s where long-term winners show up.

Our experts have identified five companies we believe could be the best buys for the current market.

They’re not the usual suspects — and that’s the point.

items.title: Item 4
items.text: My “Young Buffett” Japan Experiment -------------------------------------- Joshua Simka JOSHUA SIMKA, MARKET NEWS EDITOR In December, I decided to assemble a basket of Japanese "net-nets." The term -- from Buffett's teacher and mentor, Benjamin Graham -- refers to stocks so cheap that even if the business were to go bust tomorrow, you'd still come out ahead on the liquidation value alone. Just take a company's current assets (cash, inventory, receivables) and subtract all liabilities. That double subtraction is where the "net net" comes from: net current assets, net of total liabilities. One disclaimer up front: This was a winter-break thought experiment, not a live portfolio; I didn't actually buy any of these stocks. But I screened for and researched them as if I were going to. That turned out to be half the fun. Not so fun? My sense of regret. Because as you'll see shortly, I wish I had bought. Meet the Japanese stock that soared 453% ***************************************

items.text: Today’s Take: Stuck on the Sidelines *************************************** Sanmeet Deo It is common at our investment team meetings to discuss/pitch stocks formally or informally. items.text: Your Take ************** YESTERDAY'S TOP RESPONSE We asked, what stocks have you added to your portfolio in the last few weeks, and why?
